source.original_text: For a fixed integer n>1 and a unit vector zeta in real Euclidean n-space, the literal function P_zeta(x)=(1-||x||^2)/||x-zeta||^n is harmonic throughout R^n minus the singleton {zeta}, with x the varying argument. No value or harmonicity at the excluded pole is asserted.

lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ}, 2 ≤ n → ∀ (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), ‖a‖ = 1 →
  InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd
    (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => (1 - ‖x‖ ^ 2) / ‖x - a‖ ^ n)
    ({a}ᶜ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard l2 inner product and norm.

InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd f s means: for every x in s, f is C2 at x and its actual Euclidean Laplacian is identically zero on some neighborhood of x. The Laplacian is the orthonormal trace of the second Frechet derivative.
The set {a}ᶜ is the complement of the singleton containing a. The displayed quotient uses ordinary real division; the excluded point carries no conclusion.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.LaplacianProduct
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Basic

/-!
# The actual spherical Poisson kernel away from its unit pole

HFT, second edition, Proposition 1.18 (printed page 13 / PDF page 21),
with the source standing dimension n > 1. The kernel is the literal quotient
from Eq. 1.15, with the pole fixed and the first argument varying over its
entire complement. Factor regularity and every derivative/cancellation are
proved internally using the canonical local Laplacian product rule.

The source leaves this computation to the reader. No surface integral,
mean-value formula, Gaussian Eq. 24, TV separation or oracle bound is claimed.
-/

open Filter
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace Topology
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.PoissonKernel
set_option autoImplicit false
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
private theorem radial_fderiv {x a : E} (hx : x ≠ a) (p : ℝ) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun z : E => (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p)
      ((2 * p * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) • innerSL ℝ (x - a)) x := by
  have hn : ‖x - a‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (sub_ne_zero.mpr hx))
  have hd := (((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const a).norm_sq).rpow_const (p := p) (Or.inl hn)
  convert hd using 1
  · rfl
  · ext y
    simp [mul_assoc, mul_left_comm, mul_comm]
private theorem radial_gradient [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {x a : E} (hx : x ≠ a) (p : ℝ) :
    gradient (fun z : E => (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p) x =
      (2 * p * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) • (x - a) := by
  apply ext_inner_right ℝ
  intro y
  rw [inner_gradient_left, (radial_fderiv hx p).fderiv]
  simp [real_inner_smul_left, inner_sub_left]
private theorem radial_second {x a : E} (hx : x ≠ a) (p : ℝ) (e : E) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun z : E => fderiv ℝ (fun w : E => (‖w - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p) z e) x e =
      4 * p * (p - 1) * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 2) * (inner ℝ (x - a) e) ^ 2 +
      2 * p * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) * inner ℝ e e := by
  have hgerm : (fun z : E => fderiv ℝ (fun w : E => (‖w - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p) z e) =ᶠ[𝓝 x]
      (fun z : E => (2 * p * (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) * inner ℝ (z - a) e) := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_ne_nhds hx] with z hz
    rw [(radial_fderiv hz p).fderiv]
    simp [inner_sub_left]
  have hcoef := (radial_fderiv hx (p - 1)).const_mul (2 * p)
  have hdot := ((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const a).inner ℝ (hasFDerivAt_const e x)
  have hd := hcoef.mul hdot
  have hfd := hd.fderiv
  change fderiv ℝ (fun z : E => (2 * p * (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) * inner ℝ (z - a) e) x = _ at hfd
  rw [hgerm.fderiv_eq, hfd]
  have hp : p - 1 - 1 = p - 2 := by ring_nf
  simp [hp, smul_eq_mul, inner_sub_left]
  ring_nf
private theorem radial_laplacian [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {x a : E} (hx : x ≠ a) (p : ℝ) :
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p) x =
      4 * p * (p - 1) * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 2) * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) +
      2 * p * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  let f : E → ℝ := fun z => (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ p
  have hn : ‖x - a‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (sub_ne_zero.mpr hx))
  have hc : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x :=
    ((contDiffAt_id.sub contDiffAt_const).norm_sq ℝ).rpow_const_of_ne hn
  have hd := ((hc.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).differentiableAt one_ne_zero).hasFDerivAt
  have he (e : E) : fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x e e =
      4 * p * (p - 1) * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 2) * (inner ℝ (x - a) e) ^ 2 +
      2 * p * (‖x - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) * inner ℝ e e := by
    have hl : fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z e) x e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x e e := by
      simpa using congrArg (fun T : E →L[ℝ] ℝ => T e)
        (hd.clm_apply (hasFDerivAt_const e x)).fderiv
    rw [← hl]
    exact radial_second hx p e
  let b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E
  have ht : Laplacian.laplacian f x = ∑ i, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x (b i) (b i) := by
    rw [InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_stdOrthonormalBasis]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    rw [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply]
    rfl
  have hs : ∑ i, (inner ℝ (x - a) (b i)) ^ 2 = ‖x - a‖ ^ 2 := by
    simpa [pow_two, real_inner_comm, inner_self_eq_norm_sq] using b.sum_inner_mul_inner (x - a) (x - a)
  change Laplacian.laplacian f x = _
  rw [ht]
  simp_rw [he]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  simp only [← Finset.mul_sum]
  rw [hs]
  simp [b]
omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] in
private theorem inv_norm_pow_eq_rpow (z a : E) (n : ℕ) :
    (‖z - a‖ ^ n)⁻¹ = (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (-(n : ℝ) / 2) := by
  calc
    (‖z - a‖ ^ n)⁻¹ = ‖z - a‖ ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
      rw [Real.rpow_neg (norm_nonneg _), Real.rpow_natCast]
    _ = (‖z - a‖ ^ 2) ^ (-(n : ℝ) / 2) := by
      rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
      congr 1
      ring_nf
private theorem numerator_calculus [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (x : E) :
    gradient (fun z : E => (1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) x = (-2 : ℝ) • x ∧
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => (1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) x = (-2 : ℝ) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  constructor
  · apply ext_inner_right ℝ
    intro y
    have hd := (hasFDerivAt_const (1 : ℝ) x).sub (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt
    rw [inner_gradient_left]
    have hfd := hd.fderiv
    change fderiv ℝ (fun z : E => (1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) x = _ at hfd
    rw [hfd]
    simp [real_inner_smul_left]
  · have hd : HasFDerivAt (fderiv ℝ (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ 2))
        (2 • (innerSL ℝ : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)) x := by
      rw [fderiv_norm_sq]
      exact (innerSL ℝ : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ).hasFDerivAt.const_smul 2
    have hlap : Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ 2) x = 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
      rw [InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_stdOrthonormalBasis]
      simp only [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply]
      simp [hd.fderiv, innerSL, mul_comm]
    have hC : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun _ : E => (1 : ℝ)) x := contDiffAt_const
    have hS : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ 2) x := contDiffAt_id.norm_sq ℝ
    have hfun : (fun z : E => (1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) =
        (fun _ : E => (1 : ℝ)) - (fun z : E => ‖z‖ ^ 2) := rfl
    rw [hfun, hC.laplacian_sub hS, hlap]
    simp
private theorem poisson_laplace_zero {n : ℕ} {ζ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)}
    (hζ : ‖ζ‖ = 1) (hx : x ≠ ζ) :
    Laplacian.laplacian (fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) =>
      ((1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / ‖z - ζ‖ ^ n) x = 0 := by
  let p : ℝ := -(n : ℝ) / 2
  let u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun z => 1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2
  let v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun z => (‖z - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ p
  have hn : ‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (sub_ne_zero.mpr hx))
  have hu : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 u x := contDiffAt_const.sub (contDiffAt_id.norm_sq ℝ)
  have hv : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 v x :=
    ((contDiffAt_id.sub contDiffAt_const).norm_sq ℝ).rpow_const_of_ne hn
  have hfun : (fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => ((1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / ‖z - ζ‖ ^ n) =
      fun z => u z * v z := by
    funext z
    simp only [div_eq_mul_inv, u, v, p, inv_norm_pow_eq_rpow]
  have he (q : ℝ) : (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ q = (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ (q - 1) * (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) := by
    calc
      _ = (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ ((q - 1) + 1) := by congr 1; ring_nf
      _ = _ := Real.rpow_add_one hn (q - 1)
  have hlv : Laplacian.laplacian v x = 2 * (n : ℝ) * (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1) := by
    rw [radial_laplacian hx p]
    simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
    rw [he (p - 1)]
    dsimp [p]
    ring_nf
  have hcancel : 1 - ‖x‖ ^ 2 + 2 * inner ℝ x (x - ζ) - ‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2 = 0 := by
    rw [norm_sub_sq_real]
    simp only [inner_sub_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hζ]
    ring_nf
  rw [hfun, AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.LaplacianProduct.laplacian_mul hu hv]
  rw [hlv, radial_gradient hx p, (numerator_calculus x).1, (numerator_calculus x).2]
  simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, real_inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right]
  dsimp only [u, v]
  rw [he p]
  calc
    _ = (2 * (n : ℝ) * (‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) ^ (p - 1)) *
        (1 - ‖x‖ ^ 2 + 2 * inner ℝ x (x - ζ) - ‖x - ζ‖ ^ 2) := by dsimp [p]; ring_nf
    _ = 0 := by rw [hcancel]; ring_nf
/-- HFT Proposition 1.18: the literal unit-pole Poisson kernel is harmonic
in a neighborhood of every point of the pole complement. -/
theorem poissonKernel_harmonicOnNhd {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (ζ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (hζ : ‖ζ‖ = 1) :
    InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd
      (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => (1 - ‖x‖ ^ 2) / ‖x - ζ‖ ^ n)
      ({ζ}ᶜ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) := by
  clear hn
  intro x hx
  have hne : x ≠ ζ := by simpa using hx
  constructor
  · have hu : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => (1 : ℝ) - ‖z‖ ^ 2) x :=
      contDiffAt_const.sub (contDiffAt_id.norm_sq ℝ)
    have hv : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => ‖z - ζ‖ ^ n) x :=
      ((contDiffAt_id.sub contDiffAt_const).norm ℝ (sub_ne_zero.mpr hne)).pow n
    exact hu.div hv (pow_ne_zero n (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr (sub_ne_zero.mpr hne)))
  · filter_upwards [eventually_ne_nhds hne] with z hz
    exact poisson_laplace_zero hζ hz
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Harmonic.PoissonKernel

publication_context.statement: For every integer \(n\ge2\) and fixed \(\zeta\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|\zeta\|=1\), the literal function \(P_\zeta(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)/\|x-\zeta\|^n\) is harmonic on \(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{\zeta\}\).
assumptions: \(n\) is a natural number with \(n\ge2\), exactly the book standing dimension \(n>1\). The carrier is real Euclidean \(n\)-space with its standard inner product.
The pole \(\zeta\) is fixed and satisfies \(\|\zeta\|=1\). The varying argument is \(x\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{\zeta\}\); it need not lie inside the unit ball.

The function is the literal quotient. At every point of the stated domain, \(\|x-\zeta\|>0\). Local \(C^2\) regularity is derived in the proof, not imposed as a hypothesis. No assertion is made about the excluded pole.
Lean harmonicity means local \(C^2\) regularity and vanishing actual Euclidean Laplacian on a neighborhood of every domain point. This agrees with the source notion on the open pole complement.

notation.text: Squared distance, real exponent and the two literal product factors.

steps.title: Work away from the pole
steps.text: Fix x distinct from the unit pole. The positive squared distance S permits ordinary smooth real powers, including negative powers. The polynomial numerator is smooth everywhere; both factors are C2 in a neighborhood of x.
steps.formula: S=\|x-\zeta\|^2>0,\quad p=-\frac n2,\quad u(x)=1-\|x\|^2,\quad v(x)=S^p=\|x-\zeta\|^{-n},\quad P_\zeta=uv.
steps.lean: inv_norm_pow_eq_rpow identifies the literal inverse natural power. In poisson_laplace_zero, hu and hv derive local C2 from norm-square calculus and ContDiffAt.rpow_const_of_ne.

steps.title: Differentiate the numerator
steps.text: The norm-square Frechet derivative is twice the inner-product functional. Its derivative is the constant bilinear inner product; taking an orthonormal trace gives twice the dimension. Subtracting from the constant one gives both formulas.
steps.lean: numerator_calculus uses hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq, fderiv_norm_sq, the actual Riesz-gradient pairing and the canonical orthonormal trace. It includes x=0 directly.

steps.title: Differentiate the radial factor and take its trace
steps.text: Apply the real-power chain rule to the squared distance, then differentiate in a fixed direction e. Summing the diagonal second derivatives over an orthonormal basis uses Parseval. The real-power identity S^(q+1)=S^q S simplifies the result at p=-n/2.
steps.lean: radial_fderiv, radial_gradient, radial_second and radial_laplacian construct these derivatives. The trace invokes OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner. The local hlv calculation specializes p=-n/2.

steps.title: Use the canonical product rule and cancel
steps.text: Invoke the existing local Laplacian product theorem on the two actual factors. Expanding the squared distance reduces the remaining bracket to one minus the squared norm of the pole. The unit-pole source assumption makes this zero.
steps.lean: poisson_laplace_zero calls LaplacianProduct.laplacian_mul exactly once. hcancel uses norm_sub_sq_real and the unit-pole condition; the derivative identities are proved internally.

steps.title: Conclude neighborhood harmonicity
steps.text: Every point distinct from the pole has a neighborhood still avoiding it. The same computation gives zero Laplacian at every point in that neighborhood, while the literal quotient is C2 there. This establishes the source harmonicity statement on the entire pole complement.
steps.formula: \forall x\ne\zeta,\quad P_\zeta\in C^2\text{ locally at }x,\qquad\Delta P_\zeta=0\text{ on a neighborhood of }x.
steps.lean: poissonKernel_harmonicOnNhd proves the literal quotient locally C2 and uses eventually_ne_nhds together with poisson_laplace_zero. No derivative or regularity result is a public premise.

lesson.lean_statement: The exact HFT-dimension interface: a fixed unit pole and its full complement; no additional C2, derivative or Laplacian premise.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n with n >= 2 and every a in real n-dimensional Euclidean space with ||a|| = 1, the real-valued function f_a(x) = (1 - ||x||^2) / ||x - a||^n is harmonic on the complement of {a}. Precisely, for every x in real n-dimensional Euclidean space with x != a, f_a is C^2 at x and there exists a neighborhood U of x such that the actual Euclidean Laplacian of f_a is zero at every point of U. The Laplacian is the orthonormal trace of the second Frechet derivative. No conclusion is asserted at a.
